title: Phase-shifted multicomponent spin-charge nematicity in an altermagnet
authors: Christopher Candelora, Siyu Cheng, Muxian Xu, Keyu Zeng, Hengxin Tan, Younghun Hwang, Binghai Yan, Federico Mazzola, Ziqiang Wang, Ilija Zeljkovic
abstract: Altermagnets host spin-split Fermi surfaces without net magnetization. This intrinsically multicomponent electronic setting raises the possibility that familiar correlated electron phases acquire unconventional spin-charge structure. Here we report the discovery of altermagnetic nematicity in Co0.25NbSe2. Using spectroscopic-imaging scanning tunneling microscopy and spin-polarized scanning tunneling microscopy, we find that the three nominally C3-related directions lose rotational equivalence in the zero-field state, in both charge and spin-sensitive tunneling channels. Strikingly, the dominant spin-sensitive component is shifted by one C3 sector relative to the dominant charge component, revealing a phase-shifted spin-charge nematic response. A phenomenological theory shows that altermagnetic order favors a finite relative phase between the charge and spin-sensitive nematic components -- C3 lattice pinning frustrates this preferred offset and selects the observed phase locking. These results establish altermagnetic nematicity as a new form of multicomponent electronic liquid-crystal order and point to a potentially generic route by which altermagnets can transform conventional correlated phases into symmetry-engineered spin-charge orders.
summary: The paper reports finding a novel state called altermagnetic nematicity in the material $	ext{Co}_{0.25}	ext{NbSe}_2$. Using advanced STM techniques, they showed that both charge and spin electronic responses break rotational symmetry independently. Theoretically, this phase-shifted coupling is explained by the interplay between magnetic interactions and underlying crystal lattice constraints.
main_problem: The study investigates whether conventional correlated electron phases can acquire unconventional spin-charge structure when embedded within the symmetry constraints of altermagnets.
main_result: They report discovering 'altermagnetic nematicity,' a new form of multicomponent electronic liquid-crystal order characterized by a phase-shifted response between charge and spin components.
method: The research combines experimental measurements using spectroscopic-imaging scanning tunneling microscopy (STM) and spin-polarized STM with theoretical modeling based on Landau theory.
model_or_system: The physical system is $	ext{Co}_{0.25}	ext{NbSe}_2$, an altermagnet exhibiting spin-split Fermi surfaces. The theory models the nematic distortions ($\mathcal{N}_\pm$) and predicts a coupling term favoring a specific phase difference between charge-like and spin-sensitive components.
key_observables: Inequivalence of three nominally $	ext{C}_3$-related modulation peaks in both charge and spin channels, revealing a phase shift between the dominant spin and charge modulations.
important_parameters: The altermagnetic order parameter ($\Delta_A$), the crystal symmetry ($C_3$ lattice pinning), and the relative phase difference ($\varphi_\Psi - \varphi_\Phi$) between nematic components are key parameters.
main_assumptions: The authors assume that the observed offset locking is governed by a competition between the altermagnetic coupling (favoring $\pi/2$ phase shift) and the crystalline $C_3$ anisotropy.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the electronic structure, showing $2a_0$ modulations in Fourier transforms of STM maps. Diagrams are used to model the transition from higher symmetry ($	ext{C}_6$) to lower symmetry ($	ext{C}_3$) associated with the nematic state.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the electronic background (altermagnetism), then using STM/SP-STM to observe symmetry breaking in both charge and spin channels, followed by a theoretical model explaining the phase locking mechanism, culminating in the identification of altermagnetic nematicity.
why_interesting: This work provides an example of how magnetic order can engineer novel electronic symmetries (nematicity) in correlated materials, offering insights into symmetry-protected topological phases relevant to quantum matter.
